decisions.reason: As a modular successor to an already accepted trommel screen, it draws directly on the firm's established screening knowledge and is therefore highly likely to be retained and incrementally improved.

The mobile high-speed flail shredder line fits the firm's core mobile recycling machinery capabilities, service organization, and customer base, so management would usually keep learning on this related platform rather than withdraw.

A mobile high-speed grinder remains close to the firm's existing mobile processing know-how, and that relatedness gives the firm enough absorptive capacity to refine the line despite limited visible market evidence.
The stationary electric fine shredder aligns with the firm's stationary plant expertise and resource-saving direction, making continued development more plausible than exit.

The green-waste grinder is still within the firm's grinder and biomass-recycling competence base, but its narrower application and overlap with adjacent models make it the most exposed line if demand underperforms.

Stationary single-shaft pre-shredders are strongly connected to the firm's long-standing shredding and plant-engineering capabilities, so the firm is well positioned to absorb feedback and keep the product line in the portfolio.
